title: Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds out for season following meniscus tear
content:
Clemson starting quarterback Tait Reynolds will miss the rest of the Tigers’ season, the school announced Sunday, after he suffered a meniscus tear in his left knee during the Tigers’ first drive Saturday in a 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech.

Reynolds underwent surgery Sunday morning, the school said in its statement. The tear is not expected to be a long-term injury, as the surrounding ligaments are intact.

The school also announced that senior quarterback Christopher Vizzina, who started the season against LSU before the Tigers benched him for Reynolds, is in concussion protocol. Despite an ankle injury, Vizzina entered the game Saturday after the Tigers benched former walk-on Trent Pearman in Reynolds’ absence. Vizzina took a big hit during the Tigers’ final drive, and coach Dabo Swinney said during his postgame news conference that Vizzina went to the hospital. He had precautionary testing done on his neck and spine and was released later Saturday evening.

“You don’t anticipate getting to your third quarterback, but that’s what happened (Saturday),” Swinney said after one of the worst losses of his career.

“I thought he competed his butt off. I thought he competed with every ounce of everything he had. You saw what CV’s made of (Saturday).”

The injuries put the Tigers in a precarious spot at quarterback with two regular-season games left. Clemson plays at Duke on Friday and faces South Carolina on Nov. 28. The Tigers are also eligible for a postseason bowl game.

Pearman, who joined the team in 2022 and entered the 2026 season having completed just four-of-10 passes for 43 career yards, initially came in after Reynolds went down on a slide following a scramble. But after Pearman completed only two-of-six passes for 6 yards, the Tigers brought in Vizzina. Vizzina, who also dealt with an elbow injury earlier in the season, was visibly hobbling on his ankle Saturday against the Yellow Jackets. He finished the day 12-of-27 passing for 133 yards and an interception.

Reynolds finishes his first season with the program 156-of-241 passing for 1,449 yards and three touchdowns against four interceptions. The Tigers have not scored an offensive touchdown in either of their last two games, against Georgia Tech and Syracuse.

Sunday’s news only complicates things for a Clemson offense that has already had a difficult season. The Tigers rank No. 122 nationally in total offense, No. 117 in passing offense and No. 83 in rushing offense, as questions continue to swirl around offensive coordinator Chad Morris.

After an ugly loss to a Georgia Tech team that entered the weekend 2-7, Swinney — also under immense scrutiny for the Tigers’ slide — said he didn’t want to blame the loss on injuries. Still, with Reynolds out for the season and Vizzina’s status unknown, things will only get harder for Clemson.

Look for Pearman and freshman Brock Bradley to get reps. Bradley has only attempted one pass all season, a completion against Charleston Southern. If the Tigers want to get creative, quarterback-turned-receiver Chris Denson could also be an option after switching positions this offseason.

“We’ve got enough to go win the game, and we didn’t get it done,” Swinney said of Saturday’s loss. “That’s my job. So it’s really disappointing.”
